Prior to the establishment of residential schools, Indigenous children had limited access to formal education. Many communities lacked the resources and infrastructure to provide even basic educational services, leaving children to grow up without the skills and knowledge necessary to compete in the modern economy. Residential schools, on the other hand, provided a standardized education that was designed to prepare Indigenous children for integration into mainstream Canadian society.

Many Indigenous communities lacked access to basic medical services, and the spread of diseases such as tuberculosis and influenza was rampant.
